    A Product is a collection of Processes (each with its own components + cost) plus additional costs. Create one with the button above.

    Add Process
    Lower runs earlier in the WIP chain (e.g. 1, 2, 3...).
    Categorizes this process for grouping in the Processes table (e.g. Painting, Welding). Optional.
    The Warehouse Pool item this process produces per unit of output. Downstream processes consume it by referencing this exact name as a "Pool" component.
    Common Components (the process recipe — materials + qty per unit of process output, shared by every color variant; a Product can import this as a starting point and override it per product)
    Item Size Narration Source Qty / Unit Unit Remarks ✕
    Color Sub-Groups (components that only apply to one color variant of this process — e.g. a Red frame's paint vs. a Blue frame's paint. Logging a Production lot for a given color pulls in Common + that color's group only. The name doesn't have to be a Color Master entry — type any custom sub-group name instead.)
    This process has more than one independent color choice (e.g. a Base plus a separate Mudguard Color). Pick which one's checked quantities on the Production Lot form should count as the lot's total output — the others are recorded per-color but won't add to the total.
    Final stage only. This stage's output carries the whole chain's color (e.g. Black / Blue-White / Brown). Pick the one axis that identifies the product for dispatch — Ready to Dispatch then shows a separate row per value of it, named Output Item Name / value, so a specific variant can be dispatched directly instead of drilling into a combined row.
    Linked Processes (pair this process's colors one-to-one with another process's colors, e.g. this process's "Orange" with another's "Orange/White", so a downstream process consuming both from the Warehouse Pool treats them as one paired color choice instead of every combination of the two. Leave unlinked if a color like "Black" is shared with another process by coincidence and should NOT be paired.)

    Save this process first — linking needs its colors to already be known.
